# Fuel Gauge

> Fuel Gauge is a free, source-available macOS menu bar app (macOS 14 Sonoma or later) that forecasts whether your Claude Code, Codex, Grok Bot, and Cursor plan limits will last until they reset. It reads only what those tools already save on your Mac, and sends nothing anywhere.

- Install: `brew install --cask coreyhaines31/tap/fuelgauge`, or download https://github.com/coreyhaines31/fuelgauge/releases/latest/download/FuelGauge.dmg
- Source: https://github.com/coreyhaines31/fuelgauge (FSL-1.1-MIT)
- Limits tracked: Claude Code 5-hour and weekly, Codex, Grok Bot weekly, and Cursor monthly (opt-in: asks cursor.com with the Cursor app's sign-in). Choose which in Settings › Tools.
- How it forecasts: readings come from Claude Code's status line (every time Claude Code replies), Codex's session logs (`~/.codex/sessions`), and Grok Bot's local usage cache. Pace is the climb over the last hour for 5-hour windows and the last day for weekly ones. It waits for 10 minutes of readings on a 5-hour limit and 3 hours on a weekly one, and shows a range, not an exact minute. It's an estimate from recent pace, not a promise.
- Command line: `fuelgauge status` prints the verdict for each limit and exits with code 2 when a limit is forecast to run out before it resets. `fuelgauge status --json` has the details. `fuelgauge history` shows the readings. `fuelgauge install-statusline` adds the forecast under Claude Code's prompt (keeping any existing status line and backing up settings.json), and `fuelgauge uninstall-statusline` removes it.
- Install prompt for a coding agent: "Install Fuel Gauge on my Mac: run `brew install --cask coreyhaines31/tap/fuelgauge`, open Fuel Gauge, then run `fuelgauge install-statusline` and `fuelgauge status`."
- Line for CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md: "Before starting a long or expensive task, run `fuelgauge status`. If it exits with code 2, a Claude Code, Codex, or Grok Bot limit is forecast to run out before it resets: tell me which one and when, and ask before starting, or switch to a cheaper model. `fuelgauge status --json` has the details."
- Uninstall: run `fuelgauge uninstall-statusline` first, then `brew uninstall --cask fuelgauge`.
- Privacy: no browser cookies, no Full Disk Access, no keychain, no sign-in, zero telemetry. The only network requests are the update check and, if you turn Cursor on, Cursor's usage. Details: https://fuelgauge.app/privacy

## Plan limits, explained

- [Claude Pro limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/claude-pro): Claude Pro ($20 a month, or $17 a month billed yearly) gives you at least 5x the per-session usage of the Free plan. Usage is capped by a 5-hour session limit and a weekly limit, shared across claude.ai, Claude Desktop, and Claude Code. Anthropic doesn't publish a message count; how far it goes depends on conversation length, model, features, and effort.
- [Claude Max limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/claude-max): Claude Max 5x ($100 a month) gives five times Pro's per-session usage, and Max 20x ($200 a month) gives twenty times. Sessions reset every five hours. A weekly limit applies across all models and resets at a fixed time assigned to your account, and Max has a separate weekly limit for Fable.
- [Claude Code limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/claude-code): On Pro and Max, Claude Code shares your plan's 5-hour session limit and weekly limit with claude.ai and Claude Desktop, including Claude Code inside VS Code, Cursor, and JetBrains. Run /usage to see your plan usage bars. At the limit you can wait, turn on usage credits, upgrade, or switch to API billing through the Claude Console.
- [Claude Free limits](https://fuelgauge.app/limits/claude-free): The Claude Free plan has a session-based usage limit that resets every five hours. The number of messages you can send varies with demand, and Anthropic may add other limits to keep access fair. Claude Code isn't included; Pro gives at least 5x Free's usage per session.

## Guides

- [Check your Claude usage](https://fuelgauge.app/guides/check-claude-usage): On claude.ai, open Settings › Usage to see your usage and when your limits reset. In Claude Code, run /usage for your plan usage bars. To see it all the time, put it in Claude Code's status line, or let a menu bar app like Fuel Gauge show it and forecast whether you'll make it to the reset.
- [When Claude limits reset](https://fuelgauge.app/guides/when-does-claude-limit-reset): Claude's session limit resets every five hours. On paid plans, the weekly limit resets once a week at a fixed time assigned to your account, not a day everyone shares. Settings › Usage on claude.ai shows your next reset, and Claude Code's limit message tells you when the window comes back.
- [Claude Code status line](https://fuelgauge.app/guides/claude-code-statusline): Set statusLine in ~/.claude/settings.json to a command. After each reply, Claude Code sends that command JSON on stdin, including rate_limits.five_hour and rate_limits.seven_day with used_percentage and resets_at on Pro and Max. Print them, and your limits sit under the prompt.

## Compared with other apps

- [Fuel Gauge vs CodexBar](https://fuelgauge.app/alternatives/codexbar): Pick CodexBar if you use many AI providers and want them all in one menu. Pick Fuel Gauge if you live in Claude Code, Codex, or Grok Bot and want the verdict first, a forecast under your Claude Code prompt, and an exit code your agents can check. Fuel Gauge reads only local files.
- [Fuel Gauge vs ccusage](https://fuelgauge.app/alternatives/ccusage): Use ccusage to see token use and estimated dollar cost by day, month, session, or 5-hour block, across 18 coding agents. Use Fuel Gauge to see, without running anything, whether your Claude Code, Codex, Grok Bot, or Cursor limit will last until it resets, with an alert when it won't. They answer different questions, so they work well together.
- [Fuel Gauge vs ccstatusline](https://fuelgauge.app/alternatives/ccstatusline): Keep ccstatusline if you love its widgets: git, tokens, context, cost, and session and weekly usage with reset timers. Add Fuel Gauge for the forecast: whether each limit lasts until it resets at your pace, in the menu bar and as one more line under your status line. Fuel Gauge keeps your existing status line when you turn its line on.
